messages:
ops-bot: ALERT: apiserver 503s spike in eu-west-3, etcd memory OOM events x3, controller-manager queue depth rising >200
Maya (oncall): seeing the same in dashboards, apiserver p95 latency jumped to 820ms, controller-manager backlog mostly Node/Attach reconcilers
Jae: are GPU attach failures correlated? I see many AttachVolume errors in the kubelet logs for gpus in eu-west-3a
Maya (oncall): yes, attach failures + retries are flooding controller-manager. etcd logs show heavy compaction GC around same time leading to memory churn:
```
[etcd] 2023-04-12 02:43:12.123 WARN runtime: memory spike, forcing GC
[etcd] 2023-04-12 02:43:12.456 FATAL: out of memory
```
Luis: timeline wise, we had a scheduled backup job + automated compactor at 02:40 UTC. Could be overlapping with a burst of GPU provisioning from ML jobs.
Priya: eu-west-3 has limited RTX pool; we pushed a scale-out but cloud quota denied some attaches, resulting in rapid create/destroy cycles. That churn increases apiserver load and etcd write pressure
Nate: initial mitigation: pause non-critical autoscale of GPU pools, and throttle ML onboarding for 10m. Can someone patch the autoscaler policy?
Maya (oncall): I'm applying a temporary rate-limit on the autoscaler group now. Patch command:
```bash
kubectl -n infra patch configmap/gpu-autoscaler -p '{"data":{"max_attach_per_min":"8"}}'
```
Jae: also recommend disabling compactor run for 15m to reduce etcd GC pressure. Can run `etcdctl defrag` after traffic cools.
Maya (oncall): turning off compactor cronjob now. Doing `kubectl scale cronjob/etcd-compactor --replicas=0 -n kube-system`
Priya: quick cost note — pausing autoscale will push some ML jobs to queue; that'll save us transient spot/ephemeral attach costs but may delay customers. Ops to inform ML infra slack channel @ml-platform
Luis: ops-bot, create incident: short-term controlplane degradation with GPU attach churn — assign to eng-sre and ml-platform
ops-bot: Incident created INC-20230412-47 assigned to eng-sre, ml-platform
Nate: Once stabilized we should: 1) add jitter to autoscaler attach spikes, 2) add quota-aware backoff to controller-manager reconcilers (or rate limiting on provisioning controller), 3) increase etcd memory headroom on eu-west-3 controlplane nodes
Maya (oncall): agree. For immediate recovery I'll: pause autoscaler (done), disable compactor (done), throttle ML job submissions (coordinating), and escalate to infra to increase etcd node memory if we see >85% again
Jae: logs show apiserver has a lot of 429s too — consider increasing apiserver max-requests-inflight temporarily to avoid queueing at LB and instead give clearer 429s to clients
Priya: I'll DM @ml-platform with ETA for unpause and customer impact note.
Maya (oncall): monitoring: watching etcd mem, apiserver latency, controller-manager backlog; I'll update in 5m :eyes:
Luis: after rollback, we should postmortem: root cause likely autoscale quota-denied ripple + scheduled etcd maintenance windows colliding with provisioning surge. Add a runbook item to avoid compactor/backup overlap with autoscaler heavy-windows.
Maya (oncall): noted. Update: metrics trending down, etcd mem 48% -> 62% after throttles, controller backlog 200 -> 32, apiserver p95 820ms -> 160ms
Nate: Nice. Keep throttles for 10 more mins then gradual unpause.
Maya (oncall): will do. Thanks all :thumbsup:
